disclaimer: Fictional synthetic exemplars for drafting practice only. No real student data. Not legal advice.

exemplars.title: Grade 7 — Emotional Disability, peer conflict and aggression (FBA + BIP)
exemplars.profile_summary: A seventh-grade student who escalates to verbal threats and physical aggression during unstructured time and when corrected by staff, averaging 2–3 office referrals per week; FBA identified escape from perceived unfair demands and peer-status/attention.
strengths: Respects staff who are calm and consistent
exemplars.parent_concerns: Parent worries about disciplinary removals jeopardizing the school year and wants restorative rather than exclusionary responses.
evaluation_data: FBA: observations in cafeteria, hallway, and classes; interviews with staff and student
Pattern: conflict occurs most during unstructured transitions and after perceived public criticism
Rating scales elevated for conduct and emotional dysregulation across home and school
ED eligibility determined; manifestation protections apply because of repeated removals

plaafp.academic: The student is capable of grade-level work but has missed instruction due to 2–3 referrals per week and is passing only 3 of 6 classes; missing work is higher in classes following a removal.
plaafp.functional: The student misreads neutral peer/staff behavior as disrespect, escalates quickly, and lacks a repair routine after conflict. Benefits from predictable adult responses, private redirection, and structured peer interaction.
plaafp.impact: Aggression and conflict interfere with learning, peer safety, and access to the general curriculum across all classes, requiring a function-based BIP, counseling, crisis protocols, and staff consistency.

goals.condition: When frustrated with a peer or adult correction
goals.skill: use a de-escalation routine (pause, walk away, request a private conversation) without threats or physical behavior
goals.target: 8/10 events and 0 physical incidents over 6 consecutive weeks
goals.schedule: daily data; weekly review; quarterly reporting

goals.condition: Given a daily point sheet and check-in/check-out
goals.skill: attend classes and submit assigned work
goals.target: 85% submission and 5/6 passing classes by the end of the IEP year
goals.measurement: Weekly gradebook audit and point sheet

exemplars.progress_reporting: Every 9 weeks; weekly behavior point sheet sent home.
exemplars.special_factor_behavior: Behavior impedes learning and safety; FBA/BIP completed with crisis and manifestation protections.
supplementary_aids_services: Scheduled check-ins with a trusted adult before/after lunch
accommodations: Extended time on assignments after absences/removals
Reduced penalty for late work per policy during skill-building
Option to work in a quiet setting
personnel_supports: Common staff scripts for redirection and conflict
exemplars.lre_statement: The student is included in general education for all classes with behavior supports and CICO. Pull-out SEL instruction teaches replacement skills; exclusionary discipline is minimized because removals reinforce escape and reduce instructional access. Removal occurs only per code/safety with immediate return.
exemplars.placement: General education with pull-out resource services and counseling (outside regular class less than 21%).
exemplars.assessment: AASA and district assessments with extended time, small-group setting, and breaks. No alternate assessment.
exemplars.esy: Team considered ESY. The student has shown substantial regression in regulation and credit progress over the summer; ESY SEL/social skills 3x/week for 30 minutes plus academic support is recommended. Decision documented by the 45-day deadline.

behavior_support_plan.target_behavior_operational: Verbal threats, argumentative refusal, and physical aggression (e.g., pushing, grabbing) during unstructured time or following staff redirection.
behavior_support_plan.hypothesized_function: Escape from perceived unfair demands/public correction; access to peer attention/status.
antecedent_strategies: Check-in before high-risk periods (lunch, passing periods)
Restorative rather than exclusionary first response
replacement_behaviors_taught: Request a private conversation or 2-minute space
Use an 'I feel' statement and a negotiation script
consequence_strategies: Reinforce replacement behavior with points toward preferred privileges/activities
Restorative conversation and repair of harm after a conflict
Consistent, brief consequences per code paired with reteaching; avoid public power struggles
Parent contact within 24 hours for incidents
behavior_support_plan.crisis_plan: Stages: (1) agitation — offer space, reduce demands, use calm script; (2) threats — clear the area, call trained staff, avoid physical blocking unless safety requires; (3) physical behavior — follow district crisis protocol; restraint/seclusion only if imminent danger and less restrictive options insufficient, with monitoring, quick release, and same-day parent notice per §15-105. Repeated restraint/seclusion triggers plan review including FBA revision.
behavior_support_plan.progress_monitoring: Daily incident log, point sheet, weekly gradebook, monthly team data review with the student.
staff_responsibilities: All teachers: private redirection and point-sheet feedback
Behavior specialist: fidelity, data, plan revision

exemplars.notes: Middle-school aggression with manifestation considerations and restorative practice pairing.

exemplars.title: Grade 8 — Emotional Disability (anxiety), school avoidance and partial attendance
exemplars.profile_summary: An eighth-grade student with severe anxiety who has attended 60% of school days, often reporting physical symptoms in the morning and staying in the office or leaving early; academic skills are grade level when present.
strengths: Dedicated to a small group of friends
Responsive to a predictable re-entry routine
exemplars.parent_concerns: Parent is desperate to get the student back to full attendance and wants school and therapy to coordinate.
evaluation_data: Parent and teacher rating scales elevated for anxiety and school refusal behaviors
Attendance records: 60% attendance; mornings are the highest-risk period
Observation: physical complaints without medical cause; anxiety intensifies at entry and during unstructured time
ED eligibility determined based on adverse educational impact

plaafp.academic: The student is capable of grade-level work but has 40% absenteeism and incomplete work across classes; performance dropped sharply after an extended fall absence and re-entry has been difficult.
plaafp.functional: The student experiences intense anxiety entering school and attending large unstructured settings; avoids by staying in the office, arriving late, or leaving early. Social connection with a few peers is a strength.
plaafp.impact: Anxiety and avoidance behaviors prevent access to instruction and increasingly threaten credit/grade progression, requiring a graduated re-entry plan, counseling, and coordinated family/mental-health supports.

goals.condition: Given a graduated re-entry schedule and morning check-in
goals.skill: arrive at school and remain for the scheduled periods
goals.target: 90% attendance and 6 of 7 periods daily across 6 consecutive weeks
goals.schedule: daily data; weekly review; quarterly reporting

goals.condition: When anxiety peaks at entry or in unstructured settings
goals.skill: use a coping plan and request support from a designated adult instead of leaving campus
goals.target: 8/10 events without leaving the building across 4 consecutive weeks
goals.schedule: daily data; weekly review; quarterly reporting

exemplars.progress_reporting: Weekly attendance/progress communication with family; quarterly formal reports.
exemplars.special_factor_behavior: Behavior impedes learning; graduated re-entry and coping plans included. Safety monitoring is maintained in coordination with the outside provider.

services.provider: School counselor (coordinate with outside therapist with consent)

supplementary_aids_services: Graduated re-entry schedule with a designated entry/exit point
Morning check-in with a preferred adult
Copy of notes and recorded lessons for absences
accommodations: Extended time on assignments and assessments
Reduced workload during re-entry, preserving essential skills
Option to take breaks in a safe space
Alternate assessment location to reduce anxiety
personnel_supports: Staff training on school-avoidance response protocols
exemplars.lre_statement: The student is enrolled in general education with a graduated re-entry plan that increases time in classes as tolerance builds. Counseling and check-in/check-out are provided in school; supports are designed to keep the student in the least restrictive setting rather than moving to a separate program.
exemplars.placement: General education with pull-out resource services and related-service counseling (outside regular class less than 21%).
exemplars.assessment: AASA and district assessments scheduled with extended time, quiet setting, and breaks; alternate scheduling if needed. No alternate assessment.
exemplars.esy: Team considered ESY. Summer structure may prevent the severe regression seen in previous summers; ESY social/emotional programming 2x/week for 45 minutes to maintain connection and routines is recommended. Decision documented by the 45-day deadline.

behavior_support_plan.target_behavior_operational: Partial or missed attendance episodes: late arrival, remaining in the office, leaving early, or not attending classes while on campus, accompanied by physical symptom reports.
behavior_support_plan.baseline: 60% attendance; 3 of 7 periods attended; 1/10 coping-strategy use.
behavior_support_plan.hypothesized_function: Escape/avoidance of anxiety-provoking school settings and demands, with anxiety relief negatively reinforcing avoidance.
antecedent_strategies: Graduated schedule and predictable entry routine
Advance schedule preview and adjustment plans
Small-group lunch option near a trusted adult
Avoid power struggles at entry; greet and guide
replacement_behaviors_taught: Use the morning coping routine (breathing, grounding, plan review)
Request a break or safe-space visit using a card
Self-monitor with a small checklist of periods attended
Communicate distress to a designated adult before leaving
consequence_strategies: Praise/reinforce attendance and coping with a prearranged reinforcement plan
Avoid sending the student home except for valid illness/safety; return to class when possible
Neutral follow-up when periods are missed, focused on the next successful entry
behavior_support_plan.crisis_plan: If the student expresses self-harm or acute risk, follow district crisis protocol and notify the parent and counselor immediately. If the student tries to leave campus, use the agreed support plan; do not physically restrain unless imminent safety requires (A.R.S. §15-105).
behavior_support_plan.progress_monitoring: Daily attendance/period log, coping tallies, weekly counselor review, weekly family update.
staff_responsibilities: Teachers: attendance data and access to missing work
Counselor: coping plan, risk monitoring, care coordination
Case manager: data and family contact

source_lineage: PBIS Basic FBA to BSP (avoidance/escape function)
exemplars.notes: Demonstrates attendance-focused goals and graduated re-entry — a profile public exemplar IEPs almost never cover.

exemplars.title: Grade 6 — OHI/ADHD, organization across multiple classes
exemplars.profile_summary: A sixth-grade student with ADHD who is passing assessments but failing several classes due to missing work, lost materials, and slow assignment follow-through; organizational demands increased sharply with the switch to seven teachers.
exemplars.parent_concerns: Parent says the student never knows what is due and asks for a shared system across all teachers.
evaluation_data: Medical diagnosis of ADHD
Rating scales elevated for inattention and disorganization
Gradebook audit: 50% missing-work rate despite passing test averages
OHI eligibility reviewed and confirmed for continued need

plaafp.academic: The student scores at or above grade level on most assessments but is failing two classes because 50% of assignments are missing; work is often completed but not submitted.
plaafp.functional: The student has no consistent assignment-tracking system, loses materials between classes, and underestimates how long tasks take. Executive-function demands of the middle-school schedule exceed current skills.
plaafp.impact: ADHD-related organizational needs interfere with demonstrating grade-level learning and meeting middle-school expectations, requiring explicit EF instruction and system-level supports.

goals.condition: Given a shared digital assignment calendar and daily case-manager check-ins
goals.skill: record assignments and submit work on time across all classes
goals.baseline: 50% missing work; 1/5 days using the system
goals.target: 90% submission and 5/5 days using the system across 4 consecutive weeks
goals.measurement: Weekly gradebook audit and daily planner check

goals.area: Executive function — time and materials management
goals.condition: Given a class-period checklist and locker routine
goals.skill: arrive prepared and manage time for multi-step tasks
goals.schedule: daily data; weekly review; quarterly reporting

exemplars.progress_reporting: Every 9 weeks; weekly gradebook/planner updates through the parent portal.
supplementary_aids_services: Shared digital assignment calendar visible to all teachers/parents
Spare set of materials kept in the learning lab
accommodations: Extended time on assignments and assessments
personnel_supports: Cross-team agreement on assignment posting deadlines
Teacher training on ADHD-friendly assignment practices
exemplars.lre_statement: The student accesses all general education classes with organizational supports; pull-out sessions teach executive-function skills that cannot be delivered within the pacing of seven different classrooms. The design intentionally builds independence rather than adult dependence.
exemplars.placement: General education with pull-out resource services (outside regular class less than 21%).
exemplars.assessment: AASA and district assessments with extended time, low-distraction setting, and breaks. No alternate assessment.
exemplars.esy: Team considered ESY. The student showed significant regression in organizational routines and increased missing work after summer; ESY study-skills sessions 2x/week for 30 minutes with academic maintenance are recommended. Decision documented by the 45-day deadline.
exemplars.notes: Middle-school version of the EF profile; highlights system-level teacher coordination as a personnel support.

exemplars.title: Grade 4 — Autism, social skills and sensory regulation
exemplars.profile_summary: A fourth-grade student with autism who is academically on grade level but has difficulty reading social cues, joining peer play, and managing sensory overload; recess and group work are the most challenging times.
strengths: Deep interest in animals and science
exemplars.parent_concerns: Parent reports the student is lonely at recess and wants help building friendships without being singled out.
evaluation_data: Diagnostic evaluation documented autism; social communication and restricted interests identified
Speech-language evaluation: pragmatic language below age expectations
Observation: parallel play at recess; difficulty entering groups; sensory seeking/avoiding patterns
Autism eligibility determined

plaafp.academic: The student performs at grade level academically and has strong science knowledge, but written responses and group work reflect difficulty with perspective-taking and social language (e.g., one-sided explanations, missed cues).
plaafp.functional: The student engages in parallel play, has 0–1 successful peer interactions per day, and needs sensory supports (movement, noise reduction) during unstructured time to stay regulated.
plaafp.impact: Autism-related social communication and sensory needs interfere with peer relationships and with collaborative learning tasks, requiring explicit social instruction, sensory supports, and SLP services.

goals.condition: During structured recess and cooperative group work
goals.skill: initiate and maintain peer interaction using taught scripts and turn-taking
goals.measurement: Recess and group-work tallies; social skills checklist
goals.schedule: daily data; weekly review; quarterly reporting

goals.skill: use expected social language (greeting, asking questions, staying on topic, negotiating)

exemplars.progress_reporting: Every 9 weeks with social skills and SLP data; monthly parent update.
exemplars.special_factor_behavior: Sensory overload can lead to leaving the area or covering ears; sensory supports are included. No FBA needed at this time.
supplementary_aids_services: Social scripts and visual supports for joining play
Noise-reducing headphones and a quiet pass
personnel_supports: Training for recess staff on social facilitation and sensory supports
exemplars.lre_statement: The student remains in general education for all academics and much of recess, with push-in social facilitation. Pull-out sessions teach social and pragmatic skills with explicit practice; supports are delivered where peer interactions naturally occur so skills generalize.
exemplars.placement: General education with pull-out resource/speech services and push-in supports (outside regular class less than 21%).
exemplars.assessment: AASA and district assessments with extended time, visual supports, and small-group setting. No alternate assessment.
exemplars.esy: Team considered ESY. The student showed regression in social skills and increases in sensory dysregulation over summer; ESY social-skills group 2x/week for 45 minutes is recommended. Decision documented by the 45-day deadline.

behavior_support_plan.target_behavior_operational: Leaving the recess area, covering ears, or refusing group participation when noise/social demands rise.
behavior_support_plan.baseline: 3 sensory breaks/day needed; 2/10 group-entry opportunities; 0–1 peer interactions/day.
behavior_support_plan.hypothesized_function: Escape/avoidance of sensory and social overload; access to preferred solitary activity.
antecedent_strategies: Preview recess plan and identify a buddy
Offer a quieter recess option with a structured activity
Scheduled movement breaks before and after recess
replacement_behaviors_taught: Use a break card and go to the quiet spot appropriately
Ask a peer to play using a script
Notice body signals and request a sensory tool
consequence_strategies: Praise and a social-success point for using scripts/break card
Return to activity after a short regulated break when possible
behavior_support_plan.crisis_plan: If overwhelmed, guide to the quiet area; if flight risk or safety concern, use district protocol and notify the office/parent as appropriate.
behavior_support_plan.progress_monitoring: Daily recess tallies, break logs, weekly SLP/teacher review, monthly team check.
staff_responsibilities: Recess staff: facilitate peer entry, monitor break use
SPED teacher: social skills instruction and generalization
Para: push-in facilitation under teacher direction

exemplars.notes: Elementary autism with social and sensory supports; demonstrates SLP + SPED integration and push-in services.

exemplars.title: Grade 7 — Autism, social communication, self-advocacy, and anxiety
exemplars.profile_summary: A seventh-grade student with autism who is academically strong but misreads sarcasm and indirect language, dominates conversations with a special interest, and experiences anxiety when routines change; wants to make friends but struggles with give-and-take.
strengths: Good with younger students and tutoring
exemplars.parent_concerns: Parent wants the student to learn to self-advocate and read social situations without masking their identity.
evaluation_data: Autism eligibility; previous evaluation documented social communication needs
Pragmatic language evaluation: difficulty with indirect language, sarcasm, and topic maintenance
Observation: 2–3 peer conversations/day, often topic-dominated; anxiety during schedule changes
Student interview: wants friendships and to understand 'hidden rules'

plaafp.academic: The student performs above grade level in technology and science and at grade level in other subjects, but group work and oral presentations are affected by difficulty with social communication and anxiety.
plaafp.functional: The student initiates conversation 2–3 times daily but struggles with turn-taking and topic maintenance; misinterprets indirect language; needs transition warnings and self-advocacy routines.
plaafp.impact: Autism-related social communication and anxiety needs interfere with collaborative learning and peer relationships, requiring pragmatic language instruction, self-advocacy skills, and structured social opportunities.

goals.condition: During structured peer conversations and group work
goals.skill: take turns, ask follow-up questions, and maintain topic for at least 5 exchanges
goals.target: 5+ turns with 2+ follow-up questions across 3 consecutive sessions
goals.measurement: SLP conversational data and peer feedback

goals.condition: When confused, overwhelmed, or needing an accommodation
goals.skill: request clarification or support from a teacher using a script
goals.schedule: daily data; weekly review; quarterly reporting

exemplars.progress_reporting: Every 9 weeks with SLP data, self-advocacy tallies, and teacher reports.
exemplars.special_factor_behavior: Anxiety during unexpected changes; supports include advance notice and a self-regulation plan. No FBA at this time.
supplementary_aids_services: Written schedule and advance notice of changes
Social scripts for conversation and self-advocacy
Check-in with a trusted adult before high-anxiety periods
accommodations: Extended time on oral presentations and group projects
Option to work with a partner or small group rather than large group
personnel_supports: Staff training on autism-affirming supports and avoiding forced eye contact/masking
exemplars.lre_statement: The student is fully included in general education with push-in social communication supports and pull-out SLP/self-advocacy sessions. Push-in support in an elective the student enjoys provides natural peer interaction and generalization; pull-out is limited to explicit skill instruction.
exemplars.placement: General education with pull-out speech/resource services and push-in supports (outside regular class less than 21%).
exemplars.assessment: AASA and district assessments with extended time, written directions, and small-group setting. No alternate assessment.
exemplars.esy: Team considered ESY. The student regressed in pragmatic language and social routines over the prior summer; ESY social communication group 2x/week for 30 minutes with an interest-based peer activity is recommended. Decision documented by the 45-day deadline.

behavior_support_plan.target_behavior_operational: Topic-dominated conversation, missing indirect language cues, and increased anxiety/withdrawal when routines change.
behavior_support_plan.hypothesized_function: Skill deficit (social communication) plus escape/avoidance of uncertainty and sensory/social overload.
antecedent_strategies: Provide conversation topic cards and rehearsal
Offer predictable roles in group work
replacement_behaviors_taught: Ask a follow-up question after sharing a fact
Use a self-advocacy script to ask for clarification or a break
Self-monitor conversation turns with a visual
consequence_strategies: Specific praise and self-monitoring points for turn-taking and self-advocacy
Natural reinforcement through successful peer interactions and club participation
Neutral, private redirection if a conversation becomes one-sided
behavior_support_plan.crisis_plan: If anxiety escalates, offer a quiet break and grounding routine; contact a trusted adult if needed. No safety concerns identified.
behavior_support_plan.progress_monitoring: Weekly SLP data, daily self-advocacy tallies, weekly teacher check-ins, monthly team review.

exemplars.notes: Autism-affirming framing (no forced masking); self-advocacy as a goal.

exemplars.title: Grade 7 — Twice-exceptional: gifted with SLD and ADHD (underachievement profile)
exemplars.profile_summary: A seventh-grade student identified as gifted who also has dyslexia and ADHD; scores advanced on reasoning measures but writes at a third-to-fourth-grade level and is underachieving across classes due to missed work and avoidance of writing tasks.
strengths: Advanced abstract reasoning and science knowledge
exemplars.parent_concerns: Parent worries the student is being seen as 'lazy' and wants advanced content with appropriate literacy supports.
evaluation_data: Gifted identification with superior reasoning scores
SLD in written expression and basic reading; dyslexia diagnosis documented
ADHD medical diagnosis affecting sustained attention and work completion
Achievement gap between reasoning and written expression confirmed by the evaluation team

plaafp.academic: The student reasons well above grade level but writes at a third-to-fourth-grade level and reads multisyllabic words at 70% accuracy, creating a significant achievement gap. Written work is submitted for 50% of assignments; oral participation is advanced.
plaafp.functional: Avoids writing-heavy tasks, rushes or refuses long written assignments, and uses advanced verbal skills to compensate. Benefits from choice, oral demonstration of knowledge, and structured writing scaffolds.
plaafp.impact: Combined SLD (dyslexia/written expression) and ADHD needs mean the student cannot demonstrate advanced reasoning through written work, resulting in underachievement and reduced access to appropriately challenging content.

goals.condition: Given a graphic organizer, choice of topic, and speech-to-text option
goals.skill: produce organized multi-paragraph responses that demonstrate grade-level reasoning

goals.condition: Given advanced science/social studies text and morphology instruction

goals.area: Executive function — completion of challenging work
goals.condition: Given choice, chunked deadlines, and check-ins

exemplars.progress_reporting: Every 9 weeks with rubric-scored writing and gradebook data; monthly check-in with the gifted program coordinator.
exemplars.special_factor_behavior: Task avoidance stems from skill gaps and attention needs; supports focus on scaffolds and choice. No FBA at this time.
supplementary_aids_services: Advanced texts with matching scaffolds (audio + graphic organizers)
Choice of product (oral presentation, video, essay) when writing is not the target skill
accommodations: Extended time on writing and assessments
Oral responses and project-based demonstration of knowledge
personnel_supports: Joint planning between gifted and SPED staff
Assistive-technology training for the student and staff
exemplars.lre_statement: The student remains in advanced/general education classes with accommodations and pull-out SDI. The team deliberately avoids removing the student from advanced content; intervention targets the written-expression and executive-function gaps while the student continues to access appropriately challenging curriculum.
exemplars.placement: General education (including gifted services) with pull-out resource services (outside regular class less than 21%).
exemplars.assessment: AASA and district assessments with extended time, speech-to-text, and alternate response formats as permitted. No alternate assessment.
exemplars.esy: Team considered ESY. Writing and work-completion skills regressed over the prior summer; ESY writing/executive-function sessions 2x/week for 45 minutes are recommended, with optional advanced enrichment to maintain engagement. Decision documented by the 45-day deadline.
exemplars.notes: Twice-exceptional profile: the tool should warn against reducing advanced content; interventions target the disability, not the giftedness.
